pr.title: Watch subscribed pull requests from one on-demand daemon
pr.head: ac30e2a18541a32d22df78409cb7c30b5e8e938a

summary: Projector drives a pull request to a clean review with two loops, each a watcher script that an agent session keeps running: the watch loop reports review findings to the session that wrote the pull request, and the review loop reports new heads to the session that reviews it. Both poll GitHub's GraphQL API on every pass whether or not anything changed, so a busy account runs out of its 5,000 points an hour, and somebody has to start each loop by hand.

This pull request is the first layer of the plan in docs/projects/watch-daemon/readme.md. It adds one daemon per machine, project watch serve, that every project watch command starts when none runs and that exits 5 minutes after the last session goes quiet. A session subscribes to a pull request in the fix or review role. Each pass, the daemon asks GitHub one conditional REST question per pull request, which is free when the answer is 304 Not Modified, and runs GraphQL only for a pull request that changed, plus a full query every 10 minutes. It picks one owner session per pull request and role and appends what that session should do to the session's events file.

A review can move from one session to another, so project review changes too: its commands touch the review's lock as they run, the daemon treats a lock untouched for 30 minutes as a stalled review, and settle, move, and publish refuse once the lock names another session. The skills that subscribe sessions, the panel that reads the cache, and the removal of the old loops come in the layers above.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Session: one agent conversation and its subagents, named by --session, PROJECTOR_SESSION, or Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID.
  • Subscription: one line in a session's subscriptions file, such as acme/app#12 fix or acme/app review <model> <login>.
  • Live: renewed within the last 5 minutes, by Projector's mod or project watch stream.
  • Owner: the one live session that hears events for a pull request and role.
  • Review lock: <sha>.lock in the review state directory, held from setup to publish. It names the loop, which is now the session id.
  • Stalled: a lock no review command touched for watch.review_stall seconds.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The gate passes, and a live run in a scratch state directory started, raced, restarted, replaced, and idled out the daemon as the plan says.
  • One finding is open: a pass longer than a minute counts as a machine sleep, so with about 30 subscriptions no review ever stalls.
  • The § 2.6 query measures 2 GraphQL points, not 1, which doubles the plan's cost figures.

groups.title: One daemon watches every subscribed pull request
groups.kicker: src/projector/watch.py: sessions, owners, passes, the cache, and events
intro: The daemon is one loop that wakes once a second. Each turn it checks for a stop request, notes which sessions renewed, exits after 5 idle minutes, and runs a pass every watch.interval seconds, or at once when a session subscribes to something it has no result for.

1. Gather and adopt. It reads every live session's lines. A repository subscription adopts each open pull request the operator wrote or that requests the operator by login.
  2. Ask. For each pull request it sends gh api -i with If-None-Match for the pull request, its reviews page, and, when a session fixes it, the base branch.
  3. Query. A 200, a failure, an unsettled mergeable, or a full pass due runs the GraphQL query and writes the cache.
  4. Choose owners. A pull request's line beats a repository's, the newest line wins, and a fix auto line from a push never outranks an older one. A review role moves only between reviews.
  5. Announce. Each owner gets new events and reminders, each ending with the action to take.

The daemon keeps two clocks: wall time for what it records, and a monotonic clock for liveness and stalls. A gap of more than a minute between turns counts as the machine sleeping, and the daemon then counts every live session as seen and every lock as touched.

checks.text: A crash leaves nothing to clean up: the operating system drops the lock on daemon.mutex when the process ends, and the next command starts a new daemon.

files.note: The whole daemon: subscription lines, delivery, push parsing, the pass, owners, events, and starting and stopping the process.

checks.text: Open P2 finding: last_tick is set before the pass runs, so a pass longer than 60 seconds reads as a sleep and calls forgive. A full pass measured 1.8 seconds per pull request, so at about 33 subscriptions every full pass resets every lock's stall clock and no review ever stalls. The fix is to set last_tick after the pass.
Checked live: a 9.9.9 command left an unknown daemon running, and replaced a daemon whose daemon.json said 0.1.0 in 0.8 seconds. unknown never replaced either.

A lock naming the owner keeps the role with the owner until it stalls. The owner tests show the move waiting for a review in flight, a stalled lock moving to the waiting session, and a stalled lock with no other candidate coming back as NEW HEAD.

A failed or rate-limited query carries the last result forward. The ETags are saved only after a query succeeds, so the query runs again on the next pass rather than in a tight loop. Waiting for the quota reset is deferred by the plan's § 7.

groups.title: A review moves between sessions only between reviews
groups.kicker: src/projector/review.py: the lock touch, the fence, and the locked record
intro: A review's state and lock belong to the machine and the model, so a review that changed hands midway would leave the new owner locked out and let the old reviewer publish over it. These changes let the daemon tell a slow review from a dead one, and stop a reviewer that wakes after a hand-over.

• The touch. setup, census, settle, move, interdiff, and publish update the lock's modification time, and gate does every 60 seconds while it runs.
  • The fence. settle, move, and publish refuse when the lock names another loop, or is gone from a loop's review, and say it was handed over. publish checks again before each write.
  • The record. publish and copy_published write a loop's published.json under a file lock, so the daemon's copy into the new owner's record loses no entry, and the new owner's --rereview passes the collision check.

checks.text: Nothing touches the lock while a reviewer waits on a GraphQL reset or a refused publish, or reads code between commands, so 30 such minutes read as a stall. That is the open question on waiting reviewers.

files.note: Adds ReviewLock, check_lock, fence, review_locks, clear_lock, and copy_published, and calls them from each command.

checks.text: review_mutex locks the pull request's folder, whose .lock matches none of the *.lock globs that find head locks, checked against Paths.locks, review_locks, and prune.

groups.title: The project watch commands and their settings
intro: project watch adds add, remove, drop, restore, list, take, renew, stream, status, serve, and stop. Every command but serve and stop starts the daemon when none runs, and replaces one whose version is strictly older. add --from-output reads git push or gh pr create output and subscribes the session to fix auto on each pull request it shows.

Four whole-number settings join watch.auto_start: watch.interval (60, at least 30), watch.full_every (600), watch.renotify (900), and watch.review_stall (1800). The daemon reads them from the user's own configuration only. Codex's allow rule gains watch.

files.note: The watch parser and run_watch, and census, settle, interdiff, and gate now pass the loop so they reach the lock.

checks.text: Piped git push output for watch-daemon added ninjudd/projector#386 fix auto in a scratch state directory, and a branch with no open pull request added nothing.

files.note: Adds the whole-number type and its minimums, and refuses a TOML true where a number belongs.

groups.title: Tests drive the daemon with a fake gh and hand clocks
intro: tests/test_watch.py runs the daemon's pass against a fake gh that prints status lines and honors If-None-Match, with wall and monotonic clocks the test moves by hand, so a lapse, a sleep, a stall, and a full pass need no waiting. It also starts a real detached daemon and kills it. HandOverTests in tests/test_review.py covers the lock touch, the fence, and the locked record against the review module's fake GitHub.

checks.text: The full suite passes on Python 3.12: 1,258 tests, 1 skipped.

files.note: The documented settings may be whole numbers.

groups.title: The reference and the plan
intro: docs/cli.md gains a Watch pull requests section, the four settings, and the lock and fence behavior of project review. The plan moves to in-progress, corrects § 2.1 and § 2.5 where the build found the design wrong, and adds § 9.1, the choices the build settled.
